audit_statistics.AUROC: AUROC(control subgroup) - AUROC(target subgroup), single model
audit_statistics.FNR: FNR(target subgroup) - FNR(control subgroup) at threshold t, single model

design.calibration: delta = 95th percentile of the statistic over clean (rate 0) models, per (cohort, threshold)

false_positive_rates.in_sample_note: delta is the 95th percentile of the clean statistic, so the in-sample FPR is ~5% by construction; the leave-one-out figure is the honest one

conventional_absolute_rule.note: the manuscript's original absolute flag thresholds, retained for continuity; they are NOT at matched false-positive rate

headline_sentence: Across 768 audit evaluations spanning 7 cohorts, 7 architectures, 4 operating points and 13 poisoning rates, and with both audits calibrated to a common 5% false-positive rate on clean models, the subgroup-FNR audit flagged 537/768 (70%, 95% CI 0.67-0.73) against 404/768 (53%, 95% CI 0.49-0.56) for the subgroup-AUROC audit (McNemar mcnemar_chi2_cc, p=1.21e-25); restricted to attacks that actually installed, the figures were 275/287 and 210/287.
second_headline_sentence: The subgroup-AUROC audit is not strictly blind — the attack does move the subgroup-AUROC gap — but it moves it by far too little to fire a conventional audit: under the absolute flag thresholds ordinarily used (0.05 AUROC gap, 0.10 FNR gap) the AUROC audit flagged 18/287 installed attacks against 268/287 for the FNR audit.
